title: Hydrodynamization in 1D Bose gases at nonzero temperature
abstract: Hydrodynamization refers to the remarkably rapid process in relativistic heavy-ion collisions by which hydrodynamic descriptions become applicable. Following the observation of analogous behavior in ultracold one-dimensional (1D) Bose gases, hydrodynamization has been conjectured to be a universal dynamical phenomenon in quantum systems following high-energy quenches. Theoretical studies in this cold-atom setting have so far been restricted to quenches from ground states. Here we study how nonzero temperatures affect hydrodynamization. Specifically, using a homogeneous 1D gas of hard-core bosons, we explore how the initial temperature affects the timescales associated with hydrodynamization and prethermalization following a Bragg-pulse quench. We find that while the hydrodynamization coherence time remains unchanged, increasing temperature shortens both the damping time of the hydrodynamization oscillations and the prethermalization time. We argue that this is mainly the result of the broadening of the initial rapidity distribution, and introduce a nonzero-temperature dephasing time defined in terms of the extent of the rapidity distribution.
summary: This theoretical paper examines how non-zero initial temperatures influence the rapid onset of hydrodynamic behavior (hydrodynamization) and subsequent local equilibration (prethermalization) in 1D Bose gases. By analyzing the hard-core boson model after a quench, the authors find that higher temperatures accelerate these processes by broadening the initial momentum distribution. This introduces a new temperature-dependent dephasing time as a key diagnostic tool.
main_problem: The study investigates how non-zero initial temperatures affect the timescales associated with hydrodynamization and prethermalization in 1D Bose gases following a quench.
main_result: Increasing the initial temperature shortens both the damping time of hydrodynamization oscillations and the prethermalization time, which is attributed to the broadening of the initial rapidity distribution.
method: The authors use theoretical calculations, specifically analyzing the one-body density matrix for the non-interacting Fermi gas limit of the Lieb-Liniger model, which is applicable in the Tonks-Girardeau regime.
model_or_system: The system is a 1D Bose gas, modeled by the Lieb-Liniger Hamiltonian, and the analysis focuses on the homogeneous case using hard-core bosons. The dynamics are probed via a Bragg-pulse quench.
key_observables: Hydrodynamization coherence time, damping time of oscillations, prethermalization time, and the nonzero-temperature dephasing time ($	au_{dp}$).
important_parameters: Initial temperature ($T$), quench parameters (Bragg pulse), and the system's interaction regime (Tonks-Girardeau limit).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the system is nearly integrable, allowing the use of Generalized Hydrodynamics (GHD), and treats the rapidity distribution as approximately conserved in the homogeneous box trap.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the experimental sequence (Bragg pulse quench) and show the evolution of rapidity distributions for both harmonic and box traps, comparing different time regimes.
paper_structure: The paper builds upon previous ground-state studies by incorporating finite temperature effects. It details the theoretical framework for calculating one-body density matrices and then analyzes the resulting timescales for hydrodynamization and prethermalization as a function of initial temperature.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses non-equilibrium dynamics in ultracold atomic systems, providing quantitative insights into how thermal initial conditions modify universal dynamical processes like hydrodynamization, which is crucial for understanding quench dynamics in quantum simulators.
